correctness.rationale: With no labels or nested modalities, every atomic affine degree test is eventually constant, and Boolean closure gives exactly the finite/cofinite degree events. All subsets of the finite outdegree support are definable. The outdegree is Bin(n−1,lambda/n); coupling each Bernoulli(p) with Pois(p) costs p(1−exp(−p))<=p² in TV, and adding the independent mean-lambda/n term costs at most lambda/n. Comparing the same subset in both laws gives the two directed Hausdorff bounds. Truncation of binary sequences gives the closure and compactness; toggling one arbitrarily late positive digit makes every point an accumulation point. For t_J the Poisson tail starting at J, t_{j+1}/w_j=O_lambda(1/j) and −log t_J=J log J+O_lambda(J). For the least J with t_J<=epsilon, prefixes give at most 2^J cover intervals and fixing the exceptional early digits and two late indices gives at least 2^(J−1−K) separated points. The first differing weight exceeds twice the following tail and w_{J−2}/t_{J−1} tends to infinity, so one interval of length epsilon covers at most one separated point. This gives the sharp log 2 constant and zero upper box and Hausdorff dimensions, and therefore empty interior. The visible gap follows because w_0>1/2 exactly when lambda<log 2, with the two stated endpoints attainable.
